questions.question_text: In the absence of an explicit Partnership Deed, what is the legal rate of interest allowed on a partner's loan to the firm?
questions.answer: B) 6% per annum

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the nature of a Receipt and Payment Account in a Not-for-Profit Organisation?
questions.answer: B) Real Account

questions.question_text: A specific donation received towards the construction of a building by an NGO should be recorded in which financial statement?
options: A) Income side of Income and Expenditure Account
B) Asset side of the Balance Sheet
C) Liability side of the Balance Sheet
D) Expenditure side of Income and Expenditure Account
questions.answer: C) Liability side of the Balance Sheet

questions.question_text: If a new partner brings their share of goodwill in cash, the amount is credited to which account?
questions.answer: A) Premium for Goodwill Account

questions.question_text: Which formula correctly represents the Sacrificing Ratio?
questions.answer: B) Old Share - New Share

questions.question_text: At the time of admission of a partner, the balance of the General Reserve appears in the old Balance Sheet. Where should this be transferred?
options: B) All partners' capital accounts in the new ratio
C) Old partners' capital accounts in the old ratio
D) It is left untouched in the new Balance Sheet
questions.answer: C) Old partners' capital accounts in the old ratio

questions.question_text: What is the primary nature of the Revaluation Account prepared during the reconstitution of a partnership?
questions.answer: C) Nominal Account

questions.question_text: Hidden Goodwill in a partnership firm is calculated on the basis of:
options: C) Total capital of the firm based on the new partner's share minus net worth
D) Value of assets minus external liabilities
questions.answer: C) Total capital of the firm based on the new partner's share minus net worth

questions.question_text: In the event of a partner's retirement, the Gaining Ratio is used to distribute which of the following?
options: B) Retiring partner's share of goodwill
questions.answer: B) Retiring partner's share of goodwill

questions.question_text: When a partner dies during the accounting year, their share of profit up to the date of death is credited to their capital account and debited to which account?
options: B) Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
C) Profit and Loss Suspense Account
questions.answer: C) Profit and Loss Suspense Account

questions.question_text: On dissolution of a partnership firm, all assets (except cash and bank balances) are transferred to the debit side of which account?
questions.answer: B) Realisation Account

questions.question_text: How is an unrecorded liability paid at the time of dissolution recorded?
options: D) Debited to Partners' Capital Account
questions.answer: C) Debited to Realisation Account

questions.question_text: Life membership fees received by a club are considered as:
questions.answer: A) Capital Receipt

questions.question_text: If a partner is guaranteed a minimum profit and the actual profit is less than the guaranteed amount, who bears the deficiency?
options: B) The firm through Profit and Loss Account
C) The guaranteeing partners in their agreed ratio
D) It is carried forward to the next year
questions.answer: C) The guaranteeing partners in their agreed ratio

questions.question_text: If fixed amounts are withdrawn on the last day of every month, what is the average period for calculating interest on drawings?
questions.answer: C) 5.5 months

questions.question_text: A, B, and C are partners sharing profits equally. B retires. What will be the new profit-sharing ratio between A and C if nothing else is stated?
Under the capitalization of super profit method, goodwill is calculated using which formula?
options: A) Super Profit × Number of years' purchase
B) (Super Profit / Normal Rate of Return) × 100
D) Total Capital Employed - Net Worth
questions.answer: B) (Super Profit / Normal Rate of Return) × 100

questions.question_text: Which of the following items is NOT transferred to the Realisation Account on dissolution?
options: B) Profit and Loss Account (Dr. Balance)
questions.answer: B) Profit and Loss Account (Dr. Balance)

questions.question_text: In case of dissolution of a firm, a partner's loan is settled:
options: B) After paying outside liabilities but before partner's capital
questions.answer: B) After paying outside liabilities but before partner's capital

questions.question_text: Which of the following does NOT constitute a reconstitution of a partnership firm?
options: C) Dissolution of the partnership firm
D) Change in profit-sharing ratio among existing partners
questions.answer: C) Dissolution of the partnership firm

questions.question_text: Define the accounting term 'Gaining Ratio' and state when it is calculated during partnership operations. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Gaining Ratio is the ratio in which the continuing partners acquire the profit share of a retiring or deceased partner. It is calculated as Gaining Ratio = New Share - Old Share.

questions.question_text: State the primary accounting nature of the Income and Expenditure Account prepared by Not-for-Profit Organisations. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The Income and Expenditure Account is a Nominal Account. It records all revenue receipts and revenue expenses for the current accounting period on an accrual basis.

questions.question_text: What is meant by the concept of 'Hidden Goodwill' at the time of admission of a new partner? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Hidden Goodwill exists when the total implied capital of the firm, based on the new partner's capital and share, exceeds the total actual net worth of all partners.

questions.question_text: Provide one structural difference between a Revaluation Account and a Realisation Account in partnership accounting. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A Revaluation Account is prepared upon reconstitution to adjust asset/liability values, continuing the business. A Realisation Account is prepared upon dissolution to close the books and sell off assets.

questions.question_text: Partner A withdraws $10,000 at the beginning of every month for the entire year. Calculate the interest on drawings at 8% p.a. for the accounting year ending March 31. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Total drawings = 10,000 × 12 = $120,000. Average period for withdrawals at the beginning of each month is 6.5 months. Interest = 120,000 × (8/100) × (6.5/12) = $5,200.

questions.question_text: A firm's average profit is $50,000. Capital employed is $300,000 and the normal rate of return is 10%. Calculate the firm's goodwill based on 3 years' purchase of the super profit. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Normal Profit = 300,000 × 10% = $30,000. Super Profit = Average Profit - Normal Profit = 50,000 - 30,000 = $20,000. Goodwill = Super Profit × 3 = 20,000 × 3 = $60,000.

questions.question_text: Partners X and Y share profits in the ratio 3:2. Z is admitted for a 1/5th share, which he acquires equally from X and Y. Calculate the sacrificing ratio of X and Y. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Z's share is 1/5. Z acquires this equally, meaning X sacrifices 1/10 and Y sacrifices 1/10. Since both partners sacrifice equal proportions (1/10 each), their sacrificing ratio is exactly 1:1.

questions.question_text: An NPO received $100,000 as subscriptions during the year. Subscriptions outstanding at the end of the year were $20,000, and subscriptions received in advance for the next year were $10,000. Calculate the subscription income. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Total received = $100,000. Add outstanding at the end (current year income) = $20,000. Deduct advance at the end (next year's income) = $10,000. Subscription income to be credited = 100,000 + 20,000 - 10,000 = $110,000.

questions.question_text: A, B, and C are partners sharing in the ratio 3:2:1. B retires. The firm's goodwill is valued at $60,000. Pass the necessary adjustment journal entry for goodwill. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: B's share of goodwill = 60,000 × 2/6 = $20,000. A and C gain in the ratio 3:1. Debit A's Capital Account $15,000; Debit C's Capital Account $5,000; Credit B's Capital Account $20,000.

questions.question_text: Upon dissolution of a firm, partner X agreed to take over the firm's unrecorded machinery valued at $40,000 for a final settlement amount of $35,000. Pass the necessary realization journal entry. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The unrecorded asset taken over is recorded at the agreed takeover value. Journal Entry: Debit X's Capital Account $35,000; Credit Realisation Account $35,000. (Being unrecorded machinery taken over by partner X).

sections.section_name: Section D - Long Answer (LA) / Problem Solving

questions.question_text: A Sports Club has a Match Fund opening balance of $100,000. During the year, it received Match Fund donations of $20,000. Total match expenses incurred were $150,000. Detail the step-by-step accounting treatment and financial statement placement for these transactions. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Match Fund is a specific fund shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet. Opening balance = $100,000. Add: Donations = $20,000. Total Fund = $120,000. Less: Match Expenses = $120,000 (restricting to fund balance). The Fund becomes Nil. The remaining unmatched expenses of $30,000 ($150,000 - $120,000) are debited to the Income and Expenditure Account.

questions.question_text: P and Q are partners sharing profits 2:1. R is admitted for a 1/4th share and brings $50,000 as his capital. The capitals of P and Q are to be adjusted on the basis of R's capital. Calculate the new total firm capital and the adjusted capitals of P and Q. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Total capital of the new firm = R's Capital × Reciprocal of his share = 50,000 × 4 = $200,000. Remaining share for P and Q = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4. New ratio: P = (2/3) × (3/4) = 2/4; Q = (1/3) × (3/4) = 1/4; R = 1/4. Adjusted capitals: P = 200,000 × 2/4 = $100,000. Q = 200,000 × 1/4 = $50,000.

questions.question_text: Partners X, Y, and Z share profits in the ratio 5:3:2. X dies on June 30 of the current accounting year. The firm's profit for the previous year was $120,000, and profits are assumed to accrue evenly. Calculate X's share of profit till the date of death and pass the journal entry. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: X survived for 3 months (April to June). Firm's estimated profit for 3 months = 120,000 × (3/12) = $30,000. X's share of profit = 30,000 × (5/10) = $15,000. Entry: Debit Profit and Loss Suspense Account $15,000; Credit X's Capital Account $15,000. (Being deceased partner's share of profit credited).

questions.question_text: A partnership firm dissolves. Sundry Creditors amount to $50,000. An unrecorded liability of $10,000 is settled at $9,000. Additionally, the firm pays realization expenses of $2,000 on behalf of partner B, who was supposed to bear them. Pass the comprehensive realization and capital adjustment journal entries. [50-60 words]
questions.answer:
1. For payment of liabilities (Creditors + Unrecorded): Debit Realisation Account $59,000; Credit Bank/Cash Account $59,000. 
2. For realization expenses paid on behalf of partner B: Debit B's Capital Account $2,000; Credit Bank/Cash Account $2,000. This ensures B's capital is correctly reduced for the personal obligation paid by the firm.
